label: Formulated the political philosophy of the Virtuous City
description: Al-Farabi formalized the Virtuous City (Al-Madina al-Fadila) as a political organism wherein human happiness is attained through philosophical rule and prophetic illumination.
historicalContext: Composed in Baghdad and Damascus during the 10th century amidst the Abbasid renaissance, applying Greek political theory to Islamic governance.
dialecticalTension: Synthesizes Platonic utopian republicanism with Islamic prophetic leadership and active intellect cosmology.

citations.author: Al-Farabi
citations.work: Principles of the Opinions of the Citizens of the Virtuous City
citations.quote: The city in which people aim through association at that which leads to real happiness is the Virtuous City.

citations.author: Therese-Anne Druart
citations.work: Al-Farabi's Philosophy of Society and Religion

label: Transmitted and systematized Aristotelian logic and metaphysics
description: Al-Farabi earned the title 'The Second Teacher' by commenting extensively on Aristotle's Organon and reconciling Aristotelian teleology with Islamic monotheism.
historicalContext: The Greco-Arabic translation movement centered in Baghdad provided Farabi with access to the full Aristotelian corpus.
dialecticalTension: Reconciled Aristotle's eternal cosmos and prime mover with theological creation and celestial hierarchy.

citations.author: Al-Farabi
citations.quote: Logic is an instrument whose function is to direct the intellect so that it may attain truth in all intelligibles.

citations.author: Muhsin Mahdi
citations.work: Alfarabi and the Foundation of Islamic Political Philosophy

label: Provided the metaphysical key to Aristotle for Avicenna
description: Avicenna explicitly credited Al-Farabi's treatise 'On the Aims of Aristotle's Metaphysics' with enabling him to finally comprehend Aristotelian metaphysics after forty uncomprehending readings.
historicalContext: Avicenna recounts in his autobiography that he was on the verge of despairing over the Metaphysics until he purchased Farabi's treatise for three dirhams at a book market.
dialecticalTension: Provided the essential distinction between essence and existence that became foundational for Avicennian ontology.

citations.author: Avicenna (Ibn Sina)
citations.work: The Life of Ibn Sina (Sirat al-Shaykh al-Ra'is)
citations.quote: I read the Metaphysics forty times until I knew it by heart, but could not understand its aim until I found Farabi's On the Aims of the Metaphysics. Thereupon its meaning became transparent to me.

label: Guided Maimonides' philosophical logic and political theology
description: Maimonides singled out Al-Farabi's treatises as flawless works of logic and wisdom, using his political and prophetic theories in the Guide for the Perplexed.
historicalContext: In his letter to Samuel ibn Tibbon (1199), Maimonides praised Al-Farabi above all other Islamic Aristotelians.
dialecticalTension: Harmonized prophetic legislation with Aristotelian rational perfectionism.

citations.author: Moses Maimonides
citations.quote: Do not occupy yourself with books on logic except for what was composed by the wise Abu Nasr al-Farabi; all that he composed is pure flour.
